title: The Panda's Benefactor
paragraphs: “I found that child… raised her… and traveled all over looking for her real parents and family… Along the way, I got caught up in a war and was stranded for a while…”

The peacock beastman pulled out what looked like a photo album and told me the whole story in detail. Apparently, Panda was found by the peacock beastman one day, before she was even old enough to remember. Apparently, he was found tucked inside a box of goods the Peacock Beastman had ordered, as if trying to hide.

They tried to find his parents at that point but couldn’t locate them, and since he himself didn’t know much besides his name, the Peacock Beastman had no choice but to start taking care of him. At the time, the story goes, she just looked like a bear-like Demi-Human with black ears at first glance, and her identity was unknown. He explained all sorts of things—like how she had a relatively quiet personality as a child—but for me, this kind of topic makes me feel a bit sleepy.
Father is listening intently. As for me, I’m completely captivated by Sakura-chan’s sleeping face, so I’m mostly tuning it out.
“That must have been tough.”
“Lord Rasa’s life has been a series of upheavals… I’m glad this settlement seems so peaceful.”
“Yes… As for when he started fighting… well, I think it was around the time he learned various things from a fierce Hakuko warrior he met on the battlefield.”
“Hmm? The Hakuko clan?”
“Yes… going back to what I was saying earlier, Rasa’s first love was—”
Just then, we heard the sound of someone rushing over with heavy, thudding footsteps.
“Hey, what are you guys talking about?!”
“What do you mean? Lars-chan is just trying to help the Shield Hero get to know you better, isn’t she?”
“Listen, now!”
Panda is raising her voice like never before. Eventually, she looks at Father as if giving up, then sits down with her elbows propped on the table and a sulky expression on her face.
“This is getting too much of a hassle, and I hate it when Dad tells me what to do, so I’ll just say it myself.”
“I wasn’t planning on prying that deeply into it…”
“You’ve barged in this far, and yet you have the nerve to say that! You’re probably just curious about what I’ve been spending all that money on, aren’t you!”

“Well, technically speaking, that’s true… but I get that it’s not about debt. According to Elmero, the bill for Lars-chan’s tab isn’t that high, and it’s not like all the money is going back to your hometown either.”
Panda glares at the Peacock Beastman.

“Oh, well… To pick up where we left off, it was when I got caught up in a small war and ended up in an isolated town. I was saved from that crisis by a Hakuko. By chance, I ended up staying with that guy for a while. Dad, you’re still in touch with him, right?”
“Not with him personally, though.”
“Is that so?”
When Father answered, both the Panda and the Peacock Beastman nodded in unison. Then, as if to clarify, the Panda added,
“I heard he died in battle. But we’re still in touch with the people close to him.”
“Um… he was Lars-chan’s first love, right?”
“It was when she was little. I guess you could call it her first love, but since he had a wife and kids, it was never going to work out from the start.”
“Huh… From what I’ve heard, the Hakuko race is a pretty fierce people. I heard their power collapsed when Siltvelt was defeated by Melromarc.”
“Hmm. That’s what I’ve heard as well.”
Éclair agreed with Father’s reply. So they’re recognized by both Melromarc and Siltvelt, then.

“Apparently so… It seems there were all sorts of complications because they suffered a historic defeat at the hands of a wise and brilliant king. I’ve heard that the conflict that led to Father taking me in was a fallout from that very incident.”

That’s quite the story about Trash. I heard he was quite talented in the first world. And that he won several battles through strategic prowess. Back then, I was just fighting, so it felt like I beat Takt without really understanding what was going on. It seems that, in that state, Trash was competent enough to earn the trust of Father from the first world.
“And yet, the Hakuko clan still helped you?”
“I think he was a pretty mild-mannered guy compared to the rest of the Hakuko clan, don’t you? He always reminded us that brains are just as important as brute strength.”
Panda answers Father’s question in a tone that sounds slightly embarrassed.

“He certainly had charisma, too. Back then, just having him there meant we could eat and sleep in peace, even though we were in the midst of a war. The fact that we’re still alive today is probably thanks to him protecting us.”
The Peacock Beastman chimed in with the Panda’s story.
“When there wasn’t any fighting, Rasa would train with him almost every day.”
“She did look up to him, after all… He was so heroic, so dependable, and so caring.”

It really reminds me of the stories I used to hear back in Japan about seniors that the “Pig” looked up to. In most cases I’ve encountered, though, it usually ended with heartbreak, or the person turned out to be a total scoundrel—a far cry from the ideal they’d imagined. Of course, I have absolutely no intention of tarnishing Panda’s memories, nor do I mean to speak ill of the deceased.
“I see… So Lars-chan is trying to be like that person, huh?”
“Stop making fun of people!”
Panda yells at Father, but she doesn’t sound very convincing. I don’t think Father was making fun of you, though.
“…Apparently, there were suspicions that he was Tyran’s unworthy son, but I wonder what the truth really is…”
According to what I heard later, it seems to be the name of a commander from the Hakuko clan who was involved in some trouble. Old Panda added that bit of context.
“But he died, right?”

“That’s right. I heard about it quite a while after we’d parted ways. He was a general of the Hakuko Clan—one of the Four Great Clans—and apparently managed a considerable amount of land. It’s surprising that someone so strong could die so suddenly. You never know when you’ll die in battle, do you?”
Panda spoke matter-of-factly to Father, as if ruminating on the death of her beloved.
“So, here’s the main point. The fact that you’re so concerned about where my money is going has something to do with this.”
“Yeah.”
“Don’t go saying too much, okay? That goes for you, Knight, too! I’m only saying this reluctantly because I know I’ll get told off if I don’t!”
“You don’t have to be quite that careful…”
“The Shield Hero is incredibly curious, you know. I’m just making sure he doesn’t go blabbing about this in the wrong places.”
“I actually think it’d be better to keep that sort of thing from reaching the Filolial-sama’s ears.”

Éclair said this as she watched Sakura-chan snoring. The Filolial-sama are being spoken of in a bad light. But it’s true that the Filolial-sama love gossip. If Panda’s past comes to light, it’ll become common knowledge in no time. So if I argue back, it might actually make things worse for Filolial-sama. I’ll just keep my mouth shut on this one.
“Well, yeah… I get that it’s not good to spread it around too much. I do have some self-restraint.”
“I hope so, anyway.”
“Try not to talk about it too much—Lars-chan doesn’t like it. Motoyasu-kun, you know the Filolials love to gossip.”
“Boo!”
I’ll protest to Father by imitating Sakura-chan. Father looked troubled and averted his gaze from me.
“So, Lord Rasa, how does this relate to where your money is going?”
The panda looks away, clearly struggling to speak.
“As a thank-you for saving your life, you’re helping out Hakuko’s children when you have the means, right?”
The peacock beastman spoke up for the panda, who seemed reluctant to say it himself. Hmm, charity work, I see. My opinion of the panda improved just a little bit.
“I hear their mother passed away soon after. They’re apparently close siblings, but that person also mentioned that the younger sister suffers from a serious illness.”
“Ah… yeah. I know this isn’t really my style, but… when I’ve got some extra cash, I do help out a little.”
In response to the Peacock Beastman’s explanation, the Panda rattles off his reply in a rush.
“A serious illness?”

“Yeah. Apparently, it’s so serious that she has to take Yggdrasil medication twice a month or she’ll die. She had a decent inheritance, but she fell into a debt spiral in the blink of an eye and had no choice but to sell everything she could and just leave.”
“That’s a pretty grim story… So that’s why Lars-chan needs the money?”
“Through a contact—when I had some spare cash—to help cover the cost of the medicine… Don’t you dare tell anyone, okay?”

Panda threatens us, radiating as much killing intent as he can muster. It’s not scary at all. It’s probably because your room is so fancy. Besides, I’m not such a Trash that I’d go around spreading rumors like this. At most, I’ll just tattle to Father the next time we loop back.
“Helping kids who’ve lost their parents, huh… That’s admirable. How are those kids doing now?”
“Unfortunately, I’ve never even met them. I don’t even know where they are, but I’ve heard through the grapevine that they’re at least still alive.”
“That’s an unusually vague exchange for Lars-chan.”
“Shut up. It’s just like the offerings the Hero spreads around. It’s more like a little charm I perform when I have a spare moment—in between getting my hands dirty with all this dirty work! ”
Hmph—Panda crosses her arms and pouts. Seeing her like that, Father smiles gently and reaches out, stroking her cheek as if he were petting Sakura-chan.
“I’m not laughing or anything. I just thought, ‘Lars-chan really is a good person after all.’”
“Hmm, that’s a very noble way to use your resources. It’s something to be proud of.”

Father and Éclair are praising Panda’s actions. Providing financial support to the child of a first love she’s never even met—I think that’s admirable, too. Financial support, you say… Uh… I have memories of getting beaten to a pulp by Big Sister.

“To think Lord Rasa had such a story… I’m ashamed of myself for looking down on mercenaries with such a cynical eye. I believe your actions are something to be proud of—not just as a knight, but as a human being.”
“Don’t get the wrong idea, though. I do enjoy the Gathering, you know.”
“I wonder who he takes after.”
The old panda says this to the peacock Beastman, who stands with his arms crossed, tilting his head in response.
“Really, how did things come to this…”

The panda waves his hand at the two of them as if shooing them away, looking exasperated. They don’t look alike at all, so it’s impossible to tell who he takes after. In that case, it must be down to his own nature.
“So, what about the earnings from the other day?”
“A third goes here, a third goes into my pocket, and the rest… that’s how it goes, I guess.”
“I think that’s fine. Better to do a little good than none at all, right? Wait, in this case, there’s no ulterior motive, so maybe it’s actually genuine kindness?”
“That’s true. Honestly, I’m glad I’ve gotten to know Lord Rasa better since coming here.”
“I’m not into this whole ‘pretend to be best friends’ thing.”
He’s like a pig version of Ren. The fact that a miser is actually supporting a child with a serious illness makes me feel like I might actually get along with Kuro-chan.
“Hmm…”
Sakura-chan looks up with sleepy eyes.
“Good morning, Sakura-chan.”
“Hmm… Is it still nighttime?”
“Yeah, I guess so.”
“Since we’re at it, I’ll go get the bath ready.”
The peacock beastman stands up and seems to be getting ready to prepare the bath.
“Well then, I’ll go chop some firewood.”

The old panda seems to have returned to his chores as well. It makes me wonder again—at the panda’s family home, do his adoptive father and grandfather live together? It’s a strange relationship. There’s no romance there. Maybe it’s fine because the village is so lively?
“Does it seem like Lars-chan’s father runs a business in this village?”
“He travels to distant towns as a peddler while also teaching the locals here.”
“He’s a hard worker, isn’t he? What about Grandpa?”

“He farms and hunts on the side. Apparently, he used to be quite skilled at it back in the day. Whenever I’m at home, he comes over trying to make me practice—it’s such a hassle. I’m definitely going to have to practice with him tomorrow morning.”
That’s the sort of way Panda was explaining the situation at his parents’ house to Father and the others.
